summary: Both hypotheses confirmed in iteration 3. The adaptive-budget SA+ILS approach scores a consistent 87.16 (zero variance across runs), while the fixed 12-restart SA+ILS control shows 3.22-point variance (84.05–87.27) due to intermittent time-limit exceeded (TLE) on some test cases.
key_points: h-main CONFIRMED: Adaptive budget SA+ILS scored 87.16 on both runs (0 variance), meeting the ≥87.0 consistency target. This eliminates TLE-induced score drops.
h-control-negative CONFIRMED: Fixed 12-restart SA+ILS scored 84.05, 84.44, and 87.27 across three runs — a 3.22-point range — validating that TLE is the dominant source of score instability.
Trade-off is minimal: adaptive approach sacrifices only ~0.1 points of peak performance (87.16 vs 87.27 best-case) in exchange for perfect run-to-run consistency.

Current best score is 87.16. Further improvement would likely require a fundamentally stronger algorithm (e.g., semidefinite programming relaxation, longer local search with smarter time management, or population-based metaheuristics) rather than tuning the current SA+ILS framework.
